## Purpose
Direct chat completions against a Mistral model or agent, bypassing the orchestrator. It powers the Playground and the agent chat.

## Responsibilities
- **`POST /chat/completions`** returns `chat_service.chat_completion(client, data)`.
- **`POST /chat/stream`** returns SSE from `stream_chat_completion(client, data)`.
- **Request body `ChatCompletionRequest`**, aligned with Mistral's ChatCompletionRequest:
  - `model` (None means `CHAT_DEFAULT_MODEL`);
  - `messages[ChatMessage{role, content Any, name, tool_call_id, tool_calls}]`;
  - `agent_id`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `stream`, `stop`, `random_seed`;
  - `tools`, `tool_choice`, `response_format`;
  - `safe_prompt=False`, `parallel_tool_calls`.

## Key elements
The body is dumped with `exclude_none=True`, and the messages are converted to plain dicts.

## Control flow
None.

## Data, state and side effects
Calls Mistral.

## Configuration
`CHAT_DEFAULT_MODEL`.

## Interactions
- Route policy: chat.use or orchestrator.use.
- Attachments are converted for the model in `chat_service` (`services/attachments`).

## Error handling and edge cases
Errors come from the service through the global handlers.

## Nuances and gotchas
`content` is typed `Any` so that multimodal content parts (image, audio and document chunks) pass through unchanged.

## How to rebuild this file
Two handlers and two pydantic models.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_chat_playground.py` and `test_attachments.py`.
